reader.requirement: At --std 85 a USE procedure runs after an unsuccessful relative I-O operation unless an AT END or INVALID KEY phrase on the statement takes precedence: a file-name USE for its file; INPUT/OUTPUT/I-O/EXTEND for a file open in, or being opened in, that mode, except files named in another USE.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectLevel >= 2002 adds the SORT GR17 return filter; selection unchanged

reader.edition-search: grep Edition/DialectLevel/DialectBehavior in UseTierEmitter.cs, the EmitUseHook body and FileConnector.UseModeView: none; UseTierEmitter's remarks record the open-mode tier as edition-invariant (kb/Work PB344, NIST SQ137A at 1985)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: witnesses are mostly sequential files and a DELETE invalid key; not exercised on relative files: OUTPUT, I-O, EXTEND tiers, being-opened in extend mode, AT END precedence then 46

probes.printed: 4 READ RB in output mode: '  U-OUT 47'
probes.expected: GR5c: OUTPUT declarative for a file open in output mode

probes.printed: 5 READ RC key 7 with INVALID KEY: '  INVALID KEY 23' and no USE; 6 same READ with no phrase: '  U-IO 23'
probes.expected: INVALID KEY takes precedence; without it the I-O declarative runs (GR5d)

probes.printed: 7 OPEN EXTEND of an absent relative file: '  U-EXT 35'; 8 READ on a file open EXTEND: '  U-EXT 35 47'
probes.expected: GR5e: in the process of being opened in, and open in, the extend mode

probes.printed: 9 READ x2 with AT END: '  AT END 10' and no USE; third READ no phrase: '  U-IN 35 46 00', after 46
probes.expected: AT END takes precedence; the 46 READ reaches the INPUT declarative (GR5b)

probes.printed: 1 OPEN INPUT RA (absent, RA has its own USE): '  U-RA 35' only; 2 OPEN INPUT RB: '  U-IN 35 35'
probes.expected: GR5a and the 'except those files referenced by file-name-1' clause of GR5b

citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.4.8.4 GR5  (4.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5
OK  §1985:VIII.4.8.4 GR5e  (4.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5e

reader.notes: Every lettered item a-e plus the AT END and INVALID KEY precedence was probed on relative files at 85 and each selected the declarative the text names. The open-mode view answers the attempted mode during an OPEN ('being opened') and the open mode otherwise.

refuter.evidence: Attacked what the reader's probes left out: a phrase that is present but does NOT take precedence, a file in no mode, and successful statuses. Probe r5_use.cob at --std 85 (runs/r5_use-001), relative files: READ NEXT AT END on a file open OUTPUT -> '  U-OUT 47', AT END not run; random READ INVALID KEY in output mode -> '  U-OUT 47', INVALID KEY not run; WRITE INVALID KEY in input mode -> '  U-IN 48'; DELETE and REWRITE INVALID KEY in input mode -> '  U-IN 49' each; START with no phrase in I-O mode -> '  U-IO 23'; OPEN INPUT of an absent OPTIONAL file -> 05, no USE, then READ AT END 10 with the AT END taken; CLOSE of a never-opened file -> 42 and no mode declarative; READ AT END of a file opened OUTPUT and closed -> 47, neither AT END nor any mode declarative (the file is open in no mode). Each matches GR5 a-d and the precedence clause. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VIII.4.8.4 GR5  (4.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5'; 'OK  §1985:VIII.4.8.4 GR5b  (4.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5b'.
